newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax income declines in first half of 1997.
newsitem.headline: German tax income declines in first half of 1997.

text.p: Germany's income from taxes in the first half of this year declined by 2.5 percent compared to the first six months of 1996, a finance ministry spokesman said on Saturday.
The spokesman said the decline was largely due to technical reasons. Basing a prediction for tax income for the entire year on these figures would lead to false conclusions, he said.
Tax income for the month of June alone was 0.8 percent lower than in the same month in 1996, he said.
The spokesman was commenting on a report in the news magazine Der Spiegel, which also said the largest drop in income had come from self-employed taxpayers and top-earners.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government hopes strengthening economic growth may bring in more taxes and help meet the budget deficit criteria for European economic and monetary union.
The spokesman did not put a concrete figure on how much Germany had taken in from taxes in the first half of this year.
